text: Near-term projects include the Vessel Repair Facility, DARHT critical spares warehouse storage, and additional office space for technical staff. Mid-term projects include dedicated workspace for vessel inspection and staging. Advancements to the DARHT firing site optics room and to the Radiographic Support Lab (RSL) are planned for the long term. (The confinement vessels in which a hydrodynamic experiment is conducted are placed at the intersection of the centerlines of A1 and A2 within the WE.) 12 DCX STRATEGY At present, the two accelerators provide a time sequence of one to four images from A2, and one image from A1, for a total of five images that can be timed in numerous configurations. Examples include firing A1 at an earlier or later time than A2 for two-dimensional (2D) data spread out in time or firing A1 concurrently with one of the A2 pulses to provide a limited set of 3D data. Each option is important, depending on the type of data desired from the hydrodynamic experiment. The LIAs generate x-ray pulses that pass through the experi- ment and are converted to light on segmented scintillators. The light from the scintillators is captured on a GRC, trans- ferred to a computer, and recorded as a digital image. The current A1 camera utilizes an astronomy-grade integrating charge-coupled device (CCD) that records a single image, for each axis, A1 and A2.
